newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-GCM sees higher Jundee resources.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-GCM sees higher Jundee resources.

text.p: Gold producer Great Central Mines Ltd said on Wednesday that it saw clear potential for resources at its Jundee deposit in Western Australia to climb to around five million ounces from the 1.8 million estimated now.
The company's resources director Eduard Eshuys made the comment after revealing the results of deep diamond drilling at the deposit in the first quarter ending September 30 and the current quarter.
"The results so far indicate clearly the potential for Jundee to go from 1.8 million ounces to something like five million ounces in resources," Eshuys told the annual meeting.

The company's first quarter production report for the three months ended September 30 showed a major high-grade extension to the Jundee deposit, extending over a strike length of 800 metres and a verticle depth of 250 metres.
"The most recent drilling has shown there to be multiple loads similar to that which occurs in the top 100 metres which is presently being mined," the report said.
But Eshuys told shareholders that more recent drilling results showed the mineralisation extended even deeper.
"Mineralisation does extend even deeper than the 250-metre depth that we have got results for, so it's very clear that the mineralisation is very strong and very high grade," Eshuys said.
"It looks similar to what we have seen in the top 100 metres and I am quite confident that with effort over the next 12 to 18 months we will see these resources materialise."

Great Central's Jundee and Bronzewing mines are forecast in the current year to June 30, 1997 to produce a total of 550,000 ounces at a cash operating cost of A$250 per ounce, up from 362,000 ounces at A$255 per ounce in 1995/96.
